title: Release shotlist, schedule & ops notebook (nov 2026 draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, actionable ops notebook for the upcoming November release. Purpose: give on-call engineers and release shepherds a short 'shotlist' of the most important checks, a concise calendar for cohort ramps, and a short release-notes draft to copy into the portal. Treat as living; update during preflight and the 48h watch window.

Audience
- Release owner / conductor
- On-call SREs and stability engineers
- Product PM for release comms
- Solutions engineers running customer canaries

Snapshot (one-line)
Staged rollout across three cohorts over 6 hours: 5% -> 25% -> 100% per-region, with autoscale enabled; primary risk vector is model-routing fallbacks and token-cost spikes. Roll only during PST quiet window (03:00–09:00 UTC allowed).

Shotlist (critical, hour-by-hour)
- T-24h: final signoffs from data privacy, infra (tickets cleared), and security scan green. Confirm feature flags created and toggle names.
- T-2h: run smoke-suite (see Smoke tests section). Confirm baseline P95 latency and error baseline saved to release snapshot (document metric snapshot link in linked artifacts).
- T+0 (pilot start, cohort A = 5%): open release Slack channel (#release-2026-11-xx). Engineer on-watch acknowledges. Verify routing to new model_variant A via 100 synthetic requests. Check: model returned expected tokens and no new error codes.
- T+15m: verify token costs per request not > 2x baseline and P95 latency within +40% of baseline. If threshold exceeded, pause and scale-down or switch to variant B (fallback).
- T+45–60m: expand cohort B (25%) if signals good. If errors > 1% or sustained latency breach (P95 > +60% for 15m), trigger rollback heuristics.
- T+3h: full ramp to 100% only after a steady 90m of stable metrics post-cohort B.
- T+6h: snapshot metrics (latency, error_rate, token_cost) and enable expanded telemetry sampling for post-rollout QA.

Rollout calendar (compact)
- 2026-11-11 02:00 UTC: final preflight (dry run)
- 2026-11-12 03:00 UTC: pilot start (cohort A, 5%)
- 2026-11-12 03:45 UTC: cohort B (25%) if green
- 2026-11-12 05:15 UTC: decision point for 100% (scale to full if green)
- 2026-11-12 08:00 UTC: end watch window (move to steady telemetry cadence)
Notes: local region offsets for APAC customers: shift windows to preserve local quiet-window alignment per region owner.

Telemetry watchlist & thresholds (primary signals)
- request_error_rate (all 4xx/5xx): soft alarm at 0.8% sustained for 10m, hard alarm at 2% sustained for 5m.
- downstream_failure_rate (model fallback counts): soft 0.5% for 15m, hard 1% for 10m.
- latency_p95 (ms): soft +40% over baseline for 15m, hard +80% for 10m.
- token_cost_per_request (USD): soft +1.8x baseline for 30m, hard +3x for 15m.
- kv-cache-miss-rate: alert if > 20% uplift vs baseline; higher miss rates correlate to token cost spikes.
- trace-sampling: increase to 100% for failing requests during cohorts.

Smoke tests & validation checklist (preflight)
- API key validity and throttling: 20 parallel requests using service account, confirm rate-limits behave.
- Known prompt set: run 50 canonical prompts; check for regressions (exact string match for 70% of golden outputs; flag any hallucination increase).
- Streaming: confirm chunked streaming works for long output (>1024 tokens) on both JS and Python SDK paths.
- Auth + telemetry: confirm request shows token-level billing metadata and trace id propagation.
- Canary customers: run agreed 10-customer canaries with solutions team; collect qualitative notes.

Rollback heuristics (decision ladder)
- Fast rollback: if hard threshold hit (see Telemetry watchlist) — flip feature flag to previous model_variant, scale down new pool, and route traffic back to stable. Document the time and trigger in release channel.
- Partial rollbacks: if issue localized to a region, re-route that region to stable and continue elsewhere.
- Surge protection: if token_cost spikes without errors, enact token quota throttle policy for internal API keys and pause non-critical background requests.
- Post-rollback checklist: run smoke-suite, re-run 1:1 A/B comparison for 30m, create hotfix Jira with priority P0 if regression confirmed.

Operational quick references (short commands)
- Toggle flag (prod): ./releasectl feature toggle set rollout-2026-11 off --env=prod
- Snapshot metrics: ./telemetry snapshot create --tag release-2026-11 --window=1h
- Scale pool: ./infractl pool scale serving-new-model --replicas=0 --region=us-west1
- Route override (region): ./router override set us-east1 stable-model-2026-10 --until=\"2h\"
(Teams: don’t run infra commands unless you’re the designated operator; prefer routed overrides via release conductor.)

Communication snippets (copyable)
- Slack (announce pilot): \"Heads-up: starting pilot for release 2026-11 at 03:00 UTC. Channel #release-2026-11 open. Priya Kaur on watch; SRE on-call: Mateo. Please escalate in-channel if you observe customer impact.\"
- Status page (if degraded): \"We are investigating increased latency for text-generation endpoints. Affected customers may see slower responses. Engineers are actively rolling back the latest variant if we confirm increased errors. Updates every 30m.\"

Release notes (short draft to paste into console)
- Title: November 2026: model-routing optimizations + cost-reduction batching
- Summary: Reduced per-token CPU overhead by introducing an adaptive batching heuristic; added model-routing variant that prefers lower-latency quantized paths for short prompts. Expected net token-cost reduction ~12–18% for chat-style workloads.
- Impact: No API changes. Customers using pinned model versions are unaffected. If you use dynamic routing, you may see a latency improvement for short prompts and small token-count completions.
- Known issues: Some long-context prompts (>8k tokens) may fallback to CPU path more frequently; tracking under RD-2487.

Post-rollout sampling & QA
- Sample 10k requests across regions for semantic QA (random sample of production traffic). Run golden-pair evaluation for top-100 prompts.
- Run cost-analysis job (job id in linked_artifacts) to validate end-of-day token spend delta.
- Product-led QA: pull customer feedback for 48h via solutions-team rapid channel.

Open questions & action items
- Confirm final canary customer list (Lina to confirm by 2026-11-05).
- Concurrency stress test: need one additional GPU node in us-west1 for T+0 synthetic load (infra to provision).
- Final docs: product to publish brief release-notes page after 12:00 UTC on 2026-11-12 if rollout completes.

If anything goes sideways: follow the rollback heuristics, keep channel updates every 15 minutes, and call the incident bridge if >30 minutes recovery without improvement.

Notes to self
- This notebook borrows the 'shotlist' term from film — keep it short, prioritized. Update this doc during the dry run and stamp final timestamps after the release for the postmortem.

End of notebook
